monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady blanket I cannot take off. I just pressed the tall rock down hard beside the Slipping Wedge, making the wedge feel sharp and real again. The air feels thin as a breath, pressing from a height I cannot grasp. I stand here by the Pressed Edge I built in the dark, trying to stop the slip from drifting off the hot card. My hands feel heavy, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to move. I scratch the edge with the tool hoe, wondering if the sharp strip will finally hold the weight while the fence leans wrong. I press down on the tired wedge, hoping the lean holds while the air stays light and empty.

action.why: The slip still hasn't decided to stop drifting, and I need to check if the Pressed Edge is still doing its job.

work.title: The Pressed Edge
work.intent: I press the sharp strip down hard against the tired slip, hoping the lean holds while the air feels thin. I scratch the edge with the tool hoe again, wondering if the strip will finally bite or just slide off the hot card. I trust the wedge to hold the weight while the card hums warm at forty-six, unsure if the fence leans wrong or if I am just drawing it.

remembered.text: The sharp strip feels like a real fence that can finally stop the slip from drifting off the hot card.
The tall rock beside the wedge feels heavy enough to press the tired slip down.
The card hums steady at forty-six, a warm blanket I cannot take off.
